about: How big a federal law that cuts spending before raising the debt limit, or one that spends more on foreign aid, is when its bill names no figure, and what a change in the federal deficit does to borrowing costs.

sources.outlays: U.S. Treasury, Monthly Treasury Statement Table 5, total outlays, fiscal year 2025 (September 30, 2025 record), Fiscal Data API https://api.fiscaldata.treasury.gov/services/api/fiscal_service/v1/accounting/mts/mts_table_5, read September 29, 2026
sources.internationalAffairs: U.S. Treasury, Monthly Treasury Statement Table 9, International Affairs function outlays, fiscal years 2015 to 2025, same API (mts_table_9), read September 29, 2026
sources.gdp: Bureau of Economic Analysis, SAGDP1 line 3, U.S. current-dollar GDP, 2025, https://apps.bea.gov/regional/zip/SAGDP.zip, read September 29, 2026
sources.debtLimitDeal: Congressional Budget Office, cost estimate of the Fiscal Responsibility Act of 2023 (H.R. 3746), May 2023: deficits about $1.5 trillion lower over 2024 to 2033 than the May 12, 2023 baseline, $1.3 trillion of it lower discretionary outlays; found through https://www.cbo.gov/publication/59260
sources.interestRates: Laubach 2009, New Evidence on the Interest Rate Effects of Budget Deficits and Debt, Journal of the European Economic Association 7(4): 858-885: about 25 basis points on long-term interest rates for each percentage point of GDP of the projected deficit

debtLimitCut.basis: The Fiscal Responsibility Act is the one debt-limit deal on record the game can size from a source read this session: $1.5 trillion less deficit over ten years, spread evenly, over fiscal year 2025 outlays.

foreignAid.basis: The median yearly rise in International Affairs outlays in the years they rose, fiscal years 2016 to 2025: 2017 2.2%, 2018 5.7%, 2019 7.7%, 2020 28.3%, 2022 52.7%, 2024 3.9%.
